_meta.purpose: Public UK price benchmarks the Decarbonarma agent reasons over when sanity-checking a user's quote. Ranges are 'ballpark', not valuations. NEVER present as a guarantee that a quote is good/bad — frame as 'typical range' + 'what to question'.
_meta.vat_note: All figures are with 0% VAT on domestic solar/battery/heat-pump installs, in force until 31 March 2027. From 1 April 2027 the rate reverts to the REDUCED rate of 5% (not 20%) — add ~5% to hardware+install. EV chargers are standard-rated.
_meta.note: Real UK homeowner quotes are folded in below under 'real_uk_quotes_observed' (community quote sheets + individual quotes, mid-2026). Use those as concrete reference points alongside the public averages above.

solar_pv.unit: GBP per kW installed, MCS-certified, incl panels+inverter+scaffold+install
solar_pv.panels: Modern panels 400-450W each. ~9-10 panels per 4kW, ~13-15 per 6kW.

quote_check_flags.notes: Above ~£1,800/kW = high, push back or get another quote. Below ~£1,150/kW = check panel/inverter brand, MCS status, warranty, and whether scaffolding is really included. Economies of scale: £/kW should FALL as system grows, so a big system priced like a small one is a red flag. IMPORTANT: on larger systems (8kWp+) and competitive solar+battery bundles, real UK quotes show the panel portion at £700-1,000/kW (see real_uk_quotes_observed) — that's good value, not a red flag. Reserve the cheap-flag for small standalone systems.

battery_storage.unit: GBP per usable kWh installed (hardware + labour)
battery_storage.install_uplift: Standalone install adds £500-£1,500 depending on property/electrics.

quote_check_flags.notes: Modular installer-led systems sit at the low end; all-in-one premium units (e.g. Tesla, GivEnergy AIO) at the top. Above ~£1,000/kWh = premium — justified only by brand/warranty/integrated inverter. Compare like-for-like on USABLE kWh, not nameplate.

heat_pump_ashp.unit: GBP total installed for an air-source heat pump system (unit + cylinder + rads + labour)

ofgem_bus_average.basis: avg 8kW unit, Ofgem BUS stats Jan 2026

bus_grant_offgas_uplift.eligibility: Properties in England & Wales currently heated by oil or LPG with no mains gas connection (homes and small businesses). ASHP or GSHP via MCS-certified installer; installer applies through Ofgem and deducts at source.
bus_grant_offgas_uplift.note: £1,500 uplift on the standard £7,500. If the user is on oil or LPG heating, quote £9,000, not £7,500.

air_to_air_grant.note: Air-to-air heat pumps now BUS-eligible at £2,500 per domestic install (vs £7,500 for air-to-water/GSHP).

bus_scheme_notes.epc_requirement: Removed from April 2026 — no valid EPC needed to qualify.

quote_check_flags.notes: ALWAYS check the quote is a proper MCS install with a room-by-room heat-loss survey (MCS requires one) — a heat pump sized off a rule-of-thumb is the biggest red flag and the main cause of poor performance. Confirm the BUS grant (£7,500, or £9,000 for oil/LPG off-gas-grid homes from 21 Jul 2026) is deducted at source by the installer, not something the homeowner claims back. Watch for undersized cylinders and skipped radiator upgrades that hide behind a low headline price.

ev_charger.unit: GBP for a 7kW home charger fully installed

grant.eligibility: renters, flat owners, on-street with cross-pavement solution, landlords — NOT standard owner-occupier with driveway

quote_check_flags.notes: Above ~£1,500 (outside London/SE) = high unless a long cable run or consumer-unit upgrade is genuinely needed. Ask what's driving any premium: cable distance, earthing/PEN protection, load management, groundworks.

real_uk_quotes_observed._note: Actual UK quotes shared by homeowners (community quote sheets + individual quotes), mid-2026. Use as concrete, real-world reference points and to sanity-check — these are individual quotes, not a formal distribution. Installer names are fine to mention; no personal data.

solar_plus_battery.label: 20-panel sheet — small / independent installer
solar_plus_battery.implied: ~£1,197/kW all-in INCLUDING an 8kWh battery; the panel portion works out around £700-750/kW. Excellent value.

solar_plus_battery.label: 20-panel sheet — large / national installer (premium battery)
solar_plus_battery.implied: ~£1,899/kW all-in; the ~£5,900 premium over the small installer is almost entirely the Tesla Powerwall 3 vs a modular 8kWh battery, not extra generation.

solar_plus_battery.label: Octopus install (real homeowner, ~2025)
solar_plus_battery.extras: Zappi EV charger, bird netting, full install
solar_plus_battery.notes: Homeowner got 5 quotes ranging £11,000-£15,000 for a similar job (~36% spread). Estimated payback ~7 years. Chose a large installer for 0% finance + warranty security over a cheaper independent.

solar_plus_battery.label: Evergen quote (real homeowner)
solar_plus_battery.flag: Pricey for the size: 5.58kWp + 10kWh at £13,500 vs the small installer's 8.9kWp + 8kWh at £10,650 — a smaller system for more money. The quoted 'year-1 return £1,988 / it offsets the finance' is optimistic; recompute payback from real SEG rates and actual usage.

lessons_for_quote_checking: Always get at least 3 quotes — a real-world spread of £11k-£15k (~36%) for the same job is normal.
Small/independent installers are frequently far cheaper than large national firms for comparable solar; the big premium usually buys a Tesla Powerwall and brand/finance security, not more generation.
A premium all-in-one battery (e.g. Tesla Powerwall 3, 13.5kWh) can add ~£6k over a modular 8-10kWh battery for little extra usable benefit — compare on usable kWh.

On larger systems (8kWp+) and competitive solar+battery bundles, the panel portion can genuinely be £700-1,000/kW — that's good value, NOT 'suspiciously cheap'. The <£1,150/kW cheap-flag mainly applies to small standalone systems.
Be sceptical of headline 'year-1 return' or 'it pays for the finance' claims — they often assume high SEG rates and full self-consumption. Recompute from the buyer's real numbers.
